facts.raw_span: A 74-year-old Caucasian woman
chronic lymphocytic leukemia
complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12
receiving zanubrutinib and subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement for hypogammaglobulinemia
hospitalized for pulmonary sepsis
treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and caspofungin, with resolution
grade 4 neutropenia (<500/μL) for over 15 days
febrile peak
tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions appeared on the lower limbs and then the upper limbs
lesions progressed to central ulceration with a necrotic core
severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation with minimal necrosis, angioinvasive microbial structures, thrombosed small vessels, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells
thin-walled (5–15 μm), pauciseptate hyphae with minimal branching were seen, along with numerous thick-walled ovoid sporangia (5–20 μm) that stained strongly with PAS, GMS, and Giemsa
A 74-year-old Caucasian woman
chronic lymphocytic leukemia
complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12
receiving zanubrutinib and subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement for hypogammaglobulinemia
hospitalized for pulmonary sepsis
treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and caspofungin, with resolution
grade 4 neutropenia (<500/μL) for over 15 days
febrile peak
tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions appeared on the lower limbs and then the upper limbs
lesions progressed to central ulceration with a necrotic core
severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation with minimal necrosis, angioinvasive microbial structures, thrombosed small vessels, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells
thin-walled (5–15 μm), pauciseptate hyphae with minimal branching were seen, along with numerous thick-walled ovoid sporangia (5–20 μm) that stained strongly with PAS, GMS, and Giemsa

concepts.why: The patient's skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core, along with histopathological findings of angioinvasive microbial structures, thrombosed small vessels, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells, are consistent with mucormycosis, a rare but serious fungal infection.

The patient's grade 4 neutropenia, febrile peak, and tender skin lesions are consistent with aspergillosis, a fungal infection that can cause skin lesions and systemic illness in immunocompromised patients.
The patient's skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core could be consistent with cutaneous candidiasis, a fungal infection that can cause skin lesions in immunocompromised patients.

The patient's skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core, along with histopathological findings of severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation, could be consistent with blastomycosis, a fungal infection that can cause skin lesions and systemic illness.

The patient's grade 4 neutropenia, febrile peak, and tender skin lesions are consistent with histoplasmosis, a fungal infection that can cause skin lesions and systemic illness in immunocompromised patients.
It explains the uncovered finding of angioinvasive microbial structures and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells in the context of a complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12.

rationales.F06: Treatment with broad-spectrum antibiotics and caspofungin suggests a fungal infection, but resolution of symptoms makes it less likely to be the current diagnosis.
rationales.F07: Neutropenia increases the risk of fungal infections.
rationales.F09: Skin lesions are a common presentation of fungal infections.
rationales.F10: Progression to central ulceration with a necrotic core is consistent with a deep cutaneous fungal infection.
rationales.F11: Histopathological findings of angioinvasive microbial structures and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells are characteristic of Mucormycosis.
rationales.F12: Presence of thin-walled, pauciseptate hyphae and thick-walled ovoid sporangia is consistent with Mucormycosis.
